To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the white sugar was a commodity that was used to create a national identity, a commodity that was consumed to achieve a white society, a commodity that had the potential to become an object of commodity racism.
the consumption of white, refined sugar was a means of constructing national identity in a racially exclusive sense.
the fear of the yellow peril and the desire for white society were not merely the result of a racist mentality.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the interplay of two different forms of consumption - the consumption of commodities and the consumption of racial stereotypes - in a society that was both racially obsessed and economically dependent.
the question of how a white Australia was to be created and how the white society was to be secured.

the question of whether the white Australia policy and the sugar programme were part of a broader cultural movement, which we term ‘white Australia culture’ and which was directed at the entire population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Australian society of the first half of the twentieth century was characterised by a strong and self-confident nationalism.
sugar was a white commodity.

the Australian sugar industry, as well as the consumption of white refined sugar, were not only an economic and social issue but also a political one, and that the sugar industry and the consumption of sugar were not only a political issue but also a social and economic one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the consumption of white and white sugar became a national identity marker and a means of racial purity.
white sugar was the commodity that was consumed in the name of a white society and that the fear of the yellow peril was the ideology behind the commodity.
the white sugar campaign was an attempt to create a national identity through consumption, which in turn was supposed to lead to a racially homogeneous society.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the white sugar was a commodity that was used to convey a national identity.
commodities are not just commodities.
the white sugar industry was a central element in the formation of a white society.
